source_cards.front: What speed limit applies when the portable school signs are not out?

source_cards.front: What do red, yellow and green signal lights at intersections control?
source_cards.back: Red, yellow and green signal lights stand at many intersections to control the direction and flow of traffic.

source_cards.front: Besides motorists, who must obey traffic lights?
source_cards.back: Traffic lights bind pedestrians and bicycle and moped riders as well as motorists.

source_cards.front: What does a green light allow?
source_cards.back: A green light means you may go through the intersection in the direction the signal allows, if the roadway is clear.

source_cards.front: What does a steady yellow light warn you of?
source_cards.back: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red.

source_cards.front: May you speed up to beat a yellow light?
source_cards.back: Speeding up to beat a yellow light is illegal and could cause a crash.

source_cards.front: What must you do at a red light?
source_cards.back: On a red light, come to a complete stop before the intersection, stop line or crosswalk, and stay stopped as long as the light is red.

source_cards.front: What does a flashing red light mean?
source_cards.back: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop fully, then go on with caution when the way is clear.

source_cards.front: What does a flashing yellow light mean?
source_cards.back: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution if the roadway is clear.

source_cards.front: How does a flashing red light differ from a flashing yellow light?
source_cards.back: A flashing red light is treated as a stop sign, while a flashing yellow light only requires slowing down and proceeding with caution.

source_cards.front: What does a lighted red arrow mean?
source_cards.back: A lighted red arrow means you may not turn in its direction; stop and wait for the green signal before turning.

source_cards.front: What does a yellow arrow warn of?
source_cards.back: A yellow arrow is the warning that the arrow signal is about to turn red.

source_cards.front: What should you do facing a yellow arrow?
source_cards.back: Facing a yellow arrow, stop and wait for a green arrow if you have not entered the intersection, or finish your turn and clear it safely if you already have.

source_cards.front: Should a driver already in the intersection stop for a yellow arrow?
source_cards.back: A yellow arrow is a warning that red is next, and a driver already inside the intersection should finish the turn and clear it rather than stop.

source_cards.front: What does a flashing yellow arrow allow?
source_cards.back: A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn with caution after slowing, if the roadway is clear and you first yield to any oncoming vehicle or pedestrian.

source_cards.front: How does a red arrow differ from a flashing yellow arrow?
source_cards.back: A red arrow forbids the turn until a green signal appears, while a flashing yellow arrow permits the turn after you yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

source_cards.front: What does a green arrow allow?
source_cards.back: A green arrow, alone or with another light, lets you go in the arrow's direction if you are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.

source_cards.front: How do you treat an intersection whose signal is not working?
source_cards.back: Treat an intersection whose traffic signal is not working as a four-way stop: stop completely before entering, then go when the roadway is clear.

source_cards.front: How is an intersection with no lights or signs treated?
source_cards.back: An intersection with no traffic lights, stop signs or yield signs is treated as a four-way stop, with a full stop before entering.

source_cards.front: How are a dark signal and an uncontrolled intersection handled?
source_cards.back: A dark traffic signal and an intersection with no signals or signs at all are handled the same way, as a four-way stop.

source_cards.front: After your light turns green, whom must you still yield to?
source_cards.back: After your light turns green you must still yield to pedestrians and vehicles that are in the intersection.

source_cards.front: May you pass a vehicle that has stopped for a pedestrian?
source_cards.back: You may not pass a vehicle that has stopped for a pedestrian, even if your lane is clear or your signal is green.

source_cards.front: What do solid red lights mean at a pedestrian crosswalk signal?
source_cards.back: Solid red lights at a pedestrian crosswalk signal mean stop, because a pedestrian is in the crosswalk.

source_cards.front: What do flashing red lights mean at a pedestrian crosswalk signal?
source_cards.back: Flashing red lights at a pedestrian crosswalk signal mean stop, then go on with caution after the pedestrian has crossed the driver's half of the road.

source_cards.front: What must you attend after a conviction for running a red or flashing red light?

source_cards.front: What does the move-over law require when you pass a vehicle stopped with flashing lights?

source_cards.front: Which vehicles does the move-over law cover?

source_cards.front: What kind of vehicle does the move-over law apply to?
source_cards.back: The move-over law is about driving past a vehicle that is already pulled over at the roadside with its flashing lights on, whatever kind of vehicle it is.

source_cards.front: How does a loading school bus signal that it is stopped?

source_cards.front: How long must you stay stopped for a school bus?

source_cards.front: What two signals release you from a stopped school bus?
source_cards.back: A stopped school bus is released when it moves on or when both its stop-sign arm and flashing lights are put away.

source_cards.front: How do broken white lines differ from solid white lines?

source_cards.front: What must you do at a red light?

source_cards.front: How do you treat an intersection whose signal is not working?

source_cards.front: At a dark signal, who goes first when two vehicles arrive together?

source_cards.front: At a T intersection, which driver yields?

source_cards.front: How is an intersection with no lights or signs treated?

source_cards.front: How are a dark signal and an uncontrolled intersection handled?

source_cards.back: In fog you drive on low beams, but if you pull off the road to wait it out you turn the headlights off.

source_cards.back: Snow limits visibility, so you need your headlights on both to see and to be seen.

source_cards.front: What should you clear before driving in winter?

source_cards.front: How do your headlights help on rural roads?
source_cards.back: On rural roads, your headlights help a driver who is thinking of passing in your lane see that you are coming.

source_cards.front: What makes night driving hazardous?
source_cards.back: Reduced visibility, glare from oncoming headlights and objects you cannot see in the road combine to make night driving hazardous.

source_cards.front: When are headlights required?

source_cards.front: What lights do you use at dusk, and when does the law require headlights?
source_cards.back: At dusk you switch on headlights rather than parking lights, and from sunset to sunrise headlights are required by law.

source_cards.front: On highways, when may you use high beams?

source_cards.front: What should you do with your beams when you meet oncoming traffic?

source_cards.front: When following another car, when do you use low beams?

source_cards.back: High beams on a highway must be dimmed for an oncoming vehicle within five hundred feet, while low beams are needed within two hundred feet of a car you follow.

source_cards.back: Braking distance depends on your speed, your perception and reaction times, the pavement, your tires, your vehicle's weight including any load or trailer, and the type and condition of your brakes.

source_cards.front: A tractor-trailer blocks your view ahead. What should you do?
source_cards.back: When a large vehicle such as a tractor-trailer blocks your view ahead, drop back farther so you can see around it.

source_cards.front: Which vehicles are most at risk in wind?
source_cards.back: Wind is very dangerous for campers, large recreational vehicles and anyone towing a trailer, and it also makes lightweight vehicles harder to control.

source_cards.front: What may wind do to a vehicle pulling a trailer?
source_cards.back: Wind may make a vehicle that is pulling a trailer sway.

source_cards.front: What can wind currents cause a towing vehicle to do?
source_cards.back: Wind currents can cause a vehicle pulling a trailer to jackknife.

source_cards.front: You are towing a trailer and a truck passes on your left. What do you do?
source_cards.back: If you are towing a trailer and a truck or bus passes on your left, move as far right in your lane as you can and slow down, then speed up gently as it goes by so the trailer tracks straight.

source_cards.front: When towing as a truck passes on the left, what is the order of moves?
source_cards.back: When towing a trailer as a truck or bus passes on the left, you first move right and slow down, and then speed up only gently as it passes.

source_cards.back: Any licensed driver may move a crashed vehicle if it can run under its own power without a tow and moving it will not cause more damage or more traffic hazards.

source_cards.front: How should you follow farm machinery and other slow-moving vehicles?
source_cards.back: Behind farm machinery and other slow-moving vehicles, keep a safe following distance that gives you a good field of vision.

source_cards.front: What is the top speed of a vehicle showing the slow-moving vehicle symbol, and what should you do?
source_cards.back: A vehicle showing the slow-moving vehicle symbol on its back cannot go faster than twenty-five miles per hour, so the symbol is your signal to slow down.

source_cards.front: Does a slow-moving vehicle have a right to be on the road?
source_cards.back: A slow-moving vehicle has a legal right to be on the road, so do not grow impatient when you are behind one.

source_cards.front: How do farm machinery's usual speed and the slow-moving vehicle limit compare?
source_cards.back: Farm machinery usually travels at twenty-five miles per hour or less, while a vehicle with the slow-moving vehicle symbol can never exceed twenty-five miles per hour
